actions: Restored Pinales / Cupressaceae to Juniperus ashei in the Master Plant Pool.

family_lesson.where_to_look_first: Start with foliage plus cone type. In local Juniperus, mature foliage is mostly tiny opposite scale leaves on 3–4-angled branchlets and the seed cone is fleshy and berry-like. In Taxodium, foliage is linear/needlelike, often appearing 2-ranked on deciduous short shoots, and the seed cone is a woody globose cone.
family_lesson.strongest_field_confirmation: Aromatic/resinous conifer + simple leaves that are scale/awl-like or linear + small pollen cones + seed cones whose scale/bract units are fused; no true flowers, fruits, or arils.
core_characters: Trees or shrubs; mostly evergreen, but Taxodium is a conspicuous deciduous/cladoptosic local exception.
Bark commonly fibrous or peeling in strips/plates.
Leaves simple and may be scale-like, awl-like, or linear; arrangement can be opposite/decussate, whorled, or spiral depending on genus and shoot type.
Pollen cones are small strobili; seed cones bear exposed ovules on cone-scale complexes rather than enclosed ovaries.
Cone scales are fused with their subtending bracts in Cupressaceae.
Seed cones may be woody (Taxodium) or fleshy/berry-like (Juniperus).
There are no true fruits: a juniper 'berry' is a fleshy seed cone.
There is no aril; this helps separate Cupressaceae from Taxaceae.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not teach Cupressaceae as always evergreen; Taxodium is deciduous/seasonally cladoptosic.
Do not teach the family as always scale-leaved; Taxodium has linear leaves and Juniperus juveniles can have awl/needle-like leaves.
Do not call Juniperus seed cones berries or fruits in the botanical lesson; they are fleshy, coalesced seed cones.
Do not assume all cone scales are woody; Juniperus scales become fleshy and coalesced.
Do not keep Taxodium in a separate Taxodiaceae family in the current learner; modern treatments unite it within Cupressaceae.

fastest_cues: Mature branchlets not flattened into fanlike sprays; branchlets commonly 3–4-angled.
Adult leaves mostly opposite scale leaves; juvenile/whip leaves can be awl-like.
Seed cones small, fleshy, resinous and berry-like.
Local Ashe juniper and eastern redcedar are usually dioecious.
Juniperus.reproductive_lesson: Teach pollen cones and seed cones separately. The small pollen cones shed pollen; the blue/glaucous fleshy structures are female seed cones, not berries.

fastest_cues: Large deciduous conifer, often associated with wet sites/streams.
Linear leaves on determinate short shoots, commonly appearing in two ranks.
Whole leafy short shoots are shed seasonally.
Pollen cones occur in conspicuous pendent panicles.
Seed cones are woody, globose to ovoid, and break apart into shield-shaped cone scales.
Taxodium.reproductive_lesson: Taxodium is monoecious: pollen cones and seed cones occur on the same tree. Joey's Montezuma-cypress frames are excellent for showing pollen cones -> seed cone -> cone-scale breakup -> seeds.

fast_key: Evergreen scale foliage + tiny fleshy blue/glaucous seed cones -> Juniperus.
Deciduous linear foliage + woody round cones -> Taxodium.
Juniperus with raised hemispheric leaf glands + larger 6–9 mm dark-blue cones -> strongly supports J. ashei.
Juniperus with elliptic/elongate leaf glands + usually smaller 3–6(-7) mm blue-black/brownish-blue cones -> supports J. virginiana.
Needle bundles/fascicles or classic free-scaled pine cones -> reconsider Pinaceae.
Single seed partly surrounded by a fleshy aril -> reconsider Taxaceae.

anchor_cards.look_here_first: Inspect the scale leaves with magnification: the abaxial resin gland is distinctly raised and hemispheric, especially on whip leaves. Then confirm dark-blue 6–9 mm fleshy seed cones, usually with one seed.
confirms: Dioecious evergreen tree/shrub.
Brown bark peeling in thin strips.
Branchlets 3–4-sided.
Dark-green scale leaves 1–2 mm on mature shoots.
Raised hemispheric abaxial leaf glands.
Small pollen cones.
Dark-blue glaucous fleshy seed cones 6–9 mm, commonly 1-seeded.

anchor_cards.taxonomy_note: Current POWO accepts J. virginiana with two varieties; var. virginiana is native in Texas. Keep the project learner at species level until the local infraspecific question is reviewed.
anchor_cards.look_here_first: Compare the leaf gland and cone size with Ashe juniper. Eastern redcedar has an elliptic/elongate, not hemispherically raised, abaxial gland; its seed cones are usually smaller, about 3–6(-7) mm.
confirms: Dioecious evergreen tree, often taller and more strongly conical than Ashe juniper.
Reddish-brown bark peeling in thin strips.
Scale leaves 1–3 mm, often with acute spreading tips.
Abaxial gland elliptic or elongate rather than raised hemispheric.
Blue-black to brownish-blue glaucous fleshy seed cones 3–6(-7) mm.
Seed cones usually 1–2(-3)-seeded.

anchor_cards.look_here_first: The plant looks almost unlike a juniper: linear leaves on feathery short shoots, seasonal foliage loss, and spherical woody seed cones. The whole leafy short shoot may abscise as a unit.
confirms: Large deciduous/seasonally cladoptosic conifer.
Buttressed/swollen trunk common in wet settings; knees/pneumatophores may occur but are not mandatory.
Linear leaves commonly appearing 2-ranked on determinate short shoots.
Pollen cones in long pendent panicles.
Woody globose/ovoid seed cones about 1.5–4 cm.
Shield-shaped/peltate woody cone scales.
Monoecious reproductive system.

Pinaceae.confusion: Both are resinous conifers with woody cones.
Pinaceae.tie_breaker: Pinaceae typically has acicular/linear leaves, often in bundles or obvious needles, and cone scales are free from the bract with usually two seeds per scale. Cupressaceae scale/bract units are fused, and local Juniperus may have fleshy seed cones.

Taxaceae.tie_breaker: Taxaceae reduces the seed cone to a single seed partly or wholly surrounded by a fleshy/leathery aril. Cupressaceae lacks an aril and retains a true multi-scale seed cone, woody or fleshy.
